findings.title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: The original light value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The change makes it 70%, so the bold author link in the topic meta h5 gets much lighter and loses contrast in light themes. The dark value of `$secondary` 30% also doesn't mirror the 30% light value; it mirrors 70%. Use `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for the light value and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for the dark one.

findings.title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% for group member name
findings.body: The original light value was 30% lightness. The change makes it 50%, so the light theme gets a lighter color than before, which the request doesn't cover. Keep the light value at 30% and use 70% for the dark `$secondary` value.

findings.title: Light value changed from 70% to 30%, which darkens light-theme text
findings.body: The original light color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a faint hint color. The change makes it 30% in the light theme, so the text turns much darker than before. The desktop modal uses 70% for light and 30% for the dark `$secondary` value. Use that here.

findings.title: Light value for h3 changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original light color was 20% lightness. The change makes it 50% in the light theme, so the h3 heading gets lighter than before. The desktop equivalent uses 20% for light and `$secondary` 80% for dark. Match that.

findings.title: Light value for group member name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original light color was 30% lightness. The change makes it 50% in the light theme, so the name gets lighter than before, which the request doesn't cover. Use 30% for the light value and 70% for the dark `$secondary` value.
